summary: Druckenmiller at Bloomberg Live June 2023: long-run US entitlement/debt problem, expects hard landing and more credit casualties after 500bp of hikes, holds AI (Nvidia) longs, no fat pitch yet.

coverage.note: Debt vs fiscal gap, CBO interest projections
Bubbles history, credit/CRE/bank risks, profit decline
Hard landing timing, liquidity (BoJ, TGA, QT), AI start, sectors in recession
Politics (no claims), taxes, fat pitch/asset class flexibility
No fat pitch, patience and cash

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: since Medicare and Medicaid joined Social Security as entitlements in the 60s the seniors share of government spending had already grown dramatically safe from 30 to 58 percent of outlays
claims.claim: Demographic ageing (high 1950s birth rate, sub-2 birth rate since) plus entitlements pushes seniors' share of US outlays up, creating a long-run unfunded fiscal burden because current workers' taxes pay for seniors.
claims.indicator: seniors share of federal outlays; birth rate
claims.conditions: Long-term structural; not a 3-6 month trade
claims.testable: partly - demographic and budget data exist, but it is a decades-long thesis

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I don't think the entitlement situation is something you should be trading on in the next three to six months
claims.claim: The entitlement/debt problem is a long-term concern and not a tradable catalyst over a 3-6 month horizon.
claims.conditions: Do not trade the entitlement story short-term
claims.testable: no - explicit caution, not a signal

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: with three and a half percent unemployment we had something unprecedented we had a trillion dollar deficit
claims.claim: Deficits stayed at record levels even in booms (2018 at 3.5% unemployment, 2021), unlike past cycles where strong growth shrank the deficit, so fiscal policy has become structurally pro-cyclical-deficit.
claims.conditions: Zero interest rates masked the cost of debt
claims.testable: yes - deficit/GDP vs output gap is measurable

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: kind of suppressed what I would say is the concern about this obviously a lot of debt you're not pay any interest on it who cares but now once the inflation hit interest rates are going to go up
claims.claim: Near-zero rates suppressed concern about high debt; once inflation forced rates up, debt service becomes a binding problem.
claims.conditions: Applies when debt is large and rates rise from zero
claims.testable: yes - interest cost vs rates is measurable

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if you did your accounting like any Corporation and you assume those payments going to be made yeah the present value is probably around 200 trillion dollars
claims.claim: Official debt ($31T) ignores promised Social Security/Medicare payments; counting them as a corporation would, the present value of obligations is about $200T, so true fiscal liabilities are far larger than headline debt.
claims.indicator: present value of entitlement liabilities (~$200T vs $31T debt)
claims.conditions: Based on estimates by Kotlikoff and others
claims.testable: partly - depends on discount-rate and projection assumptions

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: it's called fiscal Gap what is fiscal Gap that's how much you would have to raise taxes today to guarantee the benefits you've promised seniors in the future it's 7.7 percent of GDP
claims.claim: The fiscal gap is 7.7% of GDP, equal to raising all taxes about 40% or cutting all spending about 36% today forever, showing the scale of unfunded promises.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: you're going to crowd out private Investments you're going to crowd out the kind of investment that made us a leader
claims.claim: Borrowing from the future via debt and entitlements crowds out private investment, harming long-run US competitiveness and reserve-currency status.
claims.direction: lower private investment, risk to reserve-currency role
claims.conditions: Long-term
claims.testable: partly - crowding out is debated empirically

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: interest expense is 27 percent of outlays by 2050 and just entitlements and interest expense just though two things alone no defense no running the government no money for the disadvantage will be 117 percent of taxes by 2050
claims.claim: CBO projections show interest expense rising from about 6% to 27% of outlays by 2050, and entitlements plus interest exceeding all tax revenue (117%) by 2050, so entitlement cuts or higher taxes are inevitable.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: every time you've had a significant asset bubble economic trouble way ahead
claims.claim: Across 500 years of documented asset bubbles, a significant bubble has been followed by economic trouble.
claims.indicator: history of asset bubbles (book The Price of Time)
claims.conditions: Needs a bubble to be identified first

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: when you had 11 years of free money um people do stupid things
claims.claim: Long periods of near-zero rates cause speculative excess (e.g. $80bn paid for Dogecoin) and suppress worry about fundamentals.
claims.conditions: Free-money regimes

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: your jack rates up 500 basis points in a year I think the probabilities would suggest that Silicon Valley Banks Bed Bath and Beyond they're probably the tip of the iceberg
claims.claim: After the biggest, broadest asset bubble and a 500bp hike in one year, bankruptcies and bank failures like SVB are likely only the first of more to come because balance sheets built under free money break when rates jump.
claims.indicator: speed of Fed tightening (bp per year)
claims.conditions: After a long easy regime followed by sharp hikes

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I could see corporate profits down 20 to 30 percent normally I would say 40 or 50 in a hard Landing but this recession is so anticipated
claims.claim: Corporate profits could fall 20-30% in this recession, less than the usual 40-50% in a hard landing, because the recession is so widely anticipated that firms are prepared.
claims.conditions: Expected recession is milder in profit terms than a surprise one
claims.testable: partly - profit drawdowns in recessions measurable

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: commercial real estate and you know I'm not informing anybody in this room with something they don't know but office is a problem
claims.claim: Commercial real estate, especially office, is a problem because remote-work lifestyle change coincides with higher financing rates.
claims.conditions: Higher financing rates plus lower office demand

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: treasuries yielding one or two percent and now they're carrying them at five so so their balance sheets are impaired but if we get in a recession then the real losses comes
claims.claim: Banks hold impaired Treasury portfolios bought at 1-2% yields after the Fed promised zero rates, and a recession would add real loan losses in credit cards and CRE, so credit tightening is likely in the next 6-9 months.
claims.indicator: bank securities unrealised losses; credit tightening
claims.conditions: If a recession occurs
claims.testable: partly - bank AOCI and lending surveys are measurable

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I haven't changed mine at all the fact that it hasn't happened yet doesn't change the probability if it does happen of the depth of it
claims.claim: A delay in recession does not lower the probability or depth of a hard landing; the lag simply pushes it out.
claims.conditions: Reasoning from stock of stimulus rather than timing

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: 10 trillion dollars 5 trillion monetary 5 trillion fiscal was put in during covid what has happened is that created this giant giant stock of liquidity
claims.claim: The $10T monetary and fiscal stimulus in COVID created a giant liquidity stock that has been worked off only slowly, delaying the downturn.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Bank of Japan changed ycc they went in and they bought 400 billion dollars worth of bonds to defend their bond market very odd situation they raise rates but then liquidity exploded on it
claims.claim: BoJ yield-curve-control defence (buying $400bn of bonds) injected global liquidity at the same time the shrinkage was meant to proceed, interrupting liquidity tightening.
claims.indicator: BoJ balance sheet purchases under YCC

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Drew down the TGA that's basically the treasury savings account from 700 billion to practically nothing last week
claims.claim: Drawing down the Treasury General Account during the debt ceiling and not issuing debt boosted liquidity, and rebuilding it (about $800bn of issuance by year end) plus QT reverses that boost.
claims.indicator: Treasury General Account balance; Treasury issuance
claims.conditions: After debt ceiling resolution
claims.testable: yes - TGA is a weekly Fed series

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: you've got the student loan thing which I think has kept consumption up that's all changing in September
claims.claim: The student loan payment pause supported consumption and its end in September removes that support.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: the FED has ended up with a higher terminal rate and in fact inflation gets stickier the long it stays in the system that it increases not decreases of probably of a hard Landing
claims.claim: The longer a hard landing is delayed, the higher the Fed's terminal rate and the stickier inflation becomes, which raises rather than lowers the odds of a hard landing.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I'm more worried about growth that I am about inflation
claims.claim: He shifted his macro focus from inflation to growth risk, expecting a downturn around end-2023 rather than Q4 2023 earlier, using anecdotal data from trucks and retail.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: we had a hard Landing in 74.75 and chemicals and oils and that stuff did great
claims.claim: In recession, some sectors (chemicals, oils in 1974-75) outperform, so there is always something to do even in a hard landing.
claims.conditions: Recession with commodity pressure

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: why can't a company like Nvidia if they go up if they go up if their orders and earnings go up 70 percent
claims.claim: A stock with rapidly rising, sustainable earnings can rise in a recession despite a high valuation, as staples do, because the market eventually prices sustained earnings.
claims.conditions: Only if earnings are sustainable; otherwise market figures it out
claims.testable: partly - earnings-momentum behaviour in recessions testable

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: AI is real it's probably it could be as transformative as the Internet
claims.claim: AI is a real secular theme comparable to the Internet, unlike crypto, so AI leaders belong in the long book.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I try and think of a situation 12 to 18 months from now based on my forecast and I think if I think the security prices are going to be less um then I short them
claims.claim: His shorting process projects the situation 12-18 months ahead and shorts securities he expects to be lower, using the same approach as for longs.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if you're dead wrong on a long you can lose a hundred percent if you're dead wrong on a short you can lose 10 times your money
claims.claim: Shorts have asymmetric downside (losses can exceed 100% of capital), and he is not sure he has ever made money on shorts in 40 years, so shorting is a game for professionals with caution on sizing.
claims.conditions: Shorting bubbles early is costly

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: in March of 99 and in three weeks covered them at a 600 million dollar loss I lost 600 million dollars on a 209 investment in three weeks
claims.claim: Shorting internet stocks in March 1999 lost $600M on $200M in three weeks even though all 12 shorts later went bankrupt: being right on a bubble but early is ruinous.
claims.conditions: Bubbles can extend far past valuation extremes

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if this is a secular move if this is if this thing is real you just don't have 10 month moves that's not how it works
claims.claim: A real secular technology move lasts years (dot-com bubble 2-2.5 years, 4 for Cisco and Sun), so Nvidia's roughly 10-month run from 100 to 380 is not unusual; he would hold for at least two or three years.
claims.conditions: If the secular thesis is correct

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: already making the top coder seven to eight times seven to eight times more productive than they were five months ago
claims.claim: AI is making top coders 7-8x more productive, which supports the thesis that AI demand is real and durable.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if I'm right it makes me more fearful of military action because that's when dictators become more dangerous is when they've got a divert attention from the immediate problem
claims.claim: A stagnating Chinese economy under Xi raises the risk of military action, as leaders divert attention from domestic problems.
claims.conditions: Absent a change in power at the top

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: what they're doing now is very stimulative we're expecting a sugar high and some kind of robust growth there maybe for six or nine months
claims.claim: Chinese stimulus will give a short sugar high of six to nine months, but long-term China will be an undynamic economy under Xi's control and not a challenge to US growth.
claims.conditions: Unless leadership changes

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: it's been the biggest value trap in history but I will say right now I I haven't checked this but it's it's by far been the the deepest breadth and the best Market uh this year
claims.claim: Japan had been a value trap for decades but in 2023 market breadth was strong because deflation seemed to be ending (nominal growth), a shareholder-value push, and a central bank behind the curve on inflation.
claims.indicator: Nikkei breadth, nominal growth, BoJ policy
claims.conditions: Deflation exit plus shareholder value reforms

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: given my record trading Japan now the last 15 years should do the opposite of what I sing mathematics
claims.claim: He jokes that his Japan trading record is poor and the opposite of his views should be done; view is tentative.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: taxes are going up it's either that or you know 30 or 40 inflation which I don't think is going to happen
claims.claim: Given the fiscal arithmetic, taxes will be much higher in about 20 years, since the alternative of 30-40% inflation is unlikely.
claims.conditions: Regardless of party in power

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I've had the luxury if there's uncertainty inequities usually that's a good time for bonds and currencies
claims.claim: Success depends on knowing when not to bet; multi-asset flexibility lets him move to bonds and currencies when equities are uncertain, as volatility in them rises when the world is blowing up.
claims.direction: rotate to bonds/FX in equity uncertainty
claims.conditions: Equity uncertainty

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I honestly don't see a fat pitch right now what I do think is given the change in liquidity giving everything I've outlined some really fat pitches are going to emerge in say the next eight to 24 months
claims.claim: He holds cash and waits: no high-conviction trade now, but liquidity changes should produce fat pitches in the next 8-24 months.
claims.conditions: Roadmap unclear; most complicated unanalyzable situation

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I don't want to blow my cash and being being a horrible mental state being down eight percent making a big bet on something that I didn't have amazing conviction on
claims.claim: Avoid making big bets while down and uncertain; preserve capital until conviction is high, since bad drawdown states lead to poor decisions.
claims.conditions: After a drawdown or when conviction is low
